summary: Provisioning now reads the clone's per-repo `git.abandon-unreachable-commits` setting between the clone step and the fetch and writes it to `false` only when the read does not already say so (clone → read → write if needed → fetch), so the fetch that deletes a merged branch's bookmark no longer abandons the branch's commits under a live issue workspace or rewrites its working copy. Fail-first on both jj binaries; the #1023 fast-follow and the docs landed in the same PR (#1080).

Generating an empty one.` on both binaries — the setting lives in the user's config directory, not the clone.

verifiedFacts: Both binaries (probe /tmp/legion-84-probe-get-v2.sh, scratch left at /tmp/legion-84-probe-get-045 and -044): `jj config get git.abandon-unreachable-commits -R <clone>` exits 0, prints `true` by default, records no operation (op log identical before and after) and takes no snapshot (an unsnapshotted loose.txt stayed unsnapshotted per `jj status --ignore-working-copy`); so the read runs WITHOUT --ignore-working-copy. `jj config set --repo … false -R <clone>` likewise records no operation and snapshots nothing; the read afterwards prints `false`.

`jj config path --repo -R <clone>` → `/home/legion/.config/jj/repos/<config-id>/config.toml` on both binaries (the daemon and panes now run as user `legion`); after the write the file holds `[git]` / `abandon-unreachable-commits = false`.

Live sighting of the window the guarded write exists for: at 19:30Z on 2026-09-13 the production clone's per-repo file `~/.config/jj/repos/834789e1326b209850cb/config.toml` read as exactly `[user]` with nothing under it (an in-place rewrite caught between truncate and write), and at 19:31:55Z it held legion-reviewer[bot]'s user.* — the shared-identity race since fixed as LEGION-44. The production clone's per-repo file today holds only user.* for legion-implementer[bot] and no git.* key, so the first provisioning after this deploys is the one that writes the key.

The workspace's colocated `.git` file still reads `gitdir: /home/ubuntu/.local/state/legion/…/.git/worktrees/legion-84` after the state dir moved to /home/legion, so `gh` (and any git command) run from inside an issue workspace fails with `not a git repository`; `gh pr create` was run from /tmp with --repo/--head/--base. jj itself is unaffected (relative .jj/repo pointer). Reported to the architect as a box fact.

trickyParts: The new-contract test's behavioural assertions (jj status, ancestors, file on disk, bookmark) are ordered before the argv assertions on purpose, so RED fails on the real symptom (`The working copy is stale`) rather than on a missing argv entry; the first provisioning's argv is captured into `firstProvisioning` and asserted at the end.

processes.test.ts's spawn pin and the fake-runner pins both expect the write because the fake runner answers empty stdout to `config get`; a real clone answers `true` (default) or `false` (already set), which is why the real-jj tests see the write once and then never.
openQuestions: The Kubernetes worker image (LEGION-24) runs under its own HOME; it needs the same config directory or its own write to see this setting — noted in the AGENTS.md bullet's scope sentence, not addressed here.
